newsitem.title: USA: Thirteen injured in balloon accident.
newsitem.headline: Thirteen injured in balloon accident.

text.p: A hot air balloon careened out of control near a highway Friday morning in north Phoenix, injuring all 13 people on board, authorities said.
The injured were transported to two area hospitals where they all were reported to be in good condition. None of the injuries are life-threatening, officials said.
Investigators said the pilot of the sightseeing balloon was trying to land at 8:09 a.m. PDT (11:09 a.m. EDT) when he hit a concrete wall and was tossed out of the balloon from the impact.
The passengers then were forced to take over and manoeuvre the balloon as it skipped across the desert landscape, coming close to Interstate 17 and high-voltage power lines.
Authorities said multi-coloured balloon finally came to rest in a vacant lot about 30 minutes later.
"The balloon bounced around a geographic area of about a mile dropping people as it went along," according to Capt. Bob Khan, a Phoenix Fire Department spokesman.
The cause of the accident was under investigation.
The passengers were in town to attend a conference at The Phoenician resort and the trip was arranged through the hotel, according to spokeswoman Sally Cooper.
Cooper said the business involved was Naturally High Balloon Co., a local outfit. The company did not return telephone calls seeking comment on the accident.
The incident is the second major balloon accident in the last five months in the Phoenix metropolitan area.

On April 15, a hot air balloon tipped over and burned as it was trying to land in a remote desert area that is a popular spot for balloonists. One woman was killed and six others were injured in the crash.
